name: Sprott Junior Uranium Miners ETF
note: ETF — included because URNJ is a central subject of this uranium-sector bookmark.
blurb: The Sprott Junior Uranium Miners ETF (URNJ) tracks the Nasdaq Sprott Junior Uranium Miners Index and targets early-stage and development-phase uranium companies — the segment commonly called junior miners or explorers. It holds approximately 35 fairly evenly weighted positions, which provides modest diversification within a universe that is by definition high-risk. Expense ratio is 0.80%, the highest in the Sprott uranium ETF family. The fund pays a dividend yield of approximately 2.25%. Energy Fuels (UUUU) is the largest single holding at over 14% of the portfolio. Junior miners offer the highest potential operating leverage to spot prices — development-stage companies can reprice dramatically when uranium spot prices rise — but also the highest idiosyncratic risk: permitting failures, financing gaps, and the 10–15-year lead time from discovery to production mean that even well-resourced juniors regularly disappoint.
recent: URNJ is positioned to benefit from uranium spot prices moving back above $100/lb in early 2026, though junior miners typically lag the initial move of a spot-price rally and outperform only if the cycle sustains. The fund underperformed both URNM and URA on a one-year trailing basis through November 2025.
